screens.title: What goes wrong?
screens.text: Insert 3, then 2, then 1 into an empty AVL tree. What happens when 1 arrives?
screens.reveal: Node 3’s left branch now has height 1 and its right branch is empty (−1): bf = −1 − 1 = −2. This is Case 1, fixed by a right rotation about 3.

screens.title: Goal
screens.text: Insert keys into an AVL tree and keep the AVL property after every insertion (LO5).

task.stem: Where does a new key go in a BST?
task.hint: This checks that you can place a new key: search for it as in a BST, and it goes in the empty branch where the search ends.

options.text: At the root, and the old root moves down
options.explanation: BST insertion never changes the root. The new key always becomes a leaf.

options.text: In the empty branch where a search for it ends: it becomes a new leaf
options.explanation: Right. AVL insertion starts exactly like this.

options.text: Next to the key closest in value, even if that node already has two children
options.explanation: The search continues until it reaches an empty branch. The new key goes there.

screens.title: The insertion procedure
points: 1. Insert the key as in a BST.
2. Backtrack towards the root, updating the balance factors.
3. Stop at the first node n with a balance factor below −1 or above +1.

4. Decide the case. bf negative (left branch too tall): if the new key is larger than n.left, it is Case 2 (LR), otherwise Case 1 (LL). bf positive: if the new key is smaller than n.right, it is Case 3 (RL), otherwise Case 4 (RR).
5. Rotate, and stop. No ancestor of n needs its balance factor changed.
screens.showRule: Insert, backtrack, stop at the first unbalanced node n, find the case, rotate once (single or double).

screens.title: Example 1 (fully worked)
screens.text: The textbook’s running example, part 1: insert 3, 2, 1, then 4 to 7 into an empty AVL tree. You can check each step in the textbook.
steps: The tree is empty, so 3 becomes the root.
2 goes in the empty left branch of 3.
1 goes in the empty left branch of 2.
Node 3 has balance factor −2: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case 1 (LL).
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
4 goes in the empty right branch of 3.
5 goes in the empty right branch of 4.
Node 3 has balance factor +2: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case 4 (RR).
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
6 goes in the empty right branch of 5.
Node 2 has balance factor +2: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case 4 (RR).
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
7 goes in the empty right branch of 6.
Node 5 has balance factor +2: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case 4 (RR).
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Example 2 (guided)
screens.text: Part 2: insert 16, 15 and 14. At each imbalance, the app pauses and asks you to click n and name the case before it continues.
steps: 16 goes in the empty right branch of 7.
15 goes in the empty left branch of 16.
Node 7 has balance factor +2: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case 3 (RL).
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.
14 goes in the empty right branch of 7.
Node 6 has balance factor +2: it is the first unbalanced node, n. Case 3 (RL).
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Example 3 (on your own)
screens.text: Part 3: insert 13, 12, 11 and 10, one at a time. After each one, build the rebalanced tree.

task.stem: Insert 13, 12, 11 and 10, one at a time, and rebalance after each insertion.
task.hint: This checks the whole insertion: insert as in a BST, update balance factors on the way up, then fix the first unbalanced node with the rotation(s) for its case.

screens.title: Why one fix is enough
screens.caption: Before 1 was inserted, the subtree rooted at 3 had height 1. After the insertion and the right rotation, the subtree (now rooted at 2) has height 1 again. Because the fixed subtree is as tall as before, nothing above it changes.

screens.title: Lesson check
screens.text: One question for each assessment criterion of this lesson’s objective. Each question allows one re-attempt, and the hint is always available.

screens.title: Summary
points: Insert as in a BST, then walk back up updating balance factors.
Fix only the first unbalanced node n, using the rotation(s) for its case.
One fix is enough: the subtree gets back its old height.
